item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 29, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Edison Research at SSRS says AM/FM radio remains the leading source of in-car audio, including among people whose primary vehicle is electric. In the latest Weekly Insights, the company compared in-car listening among Americans age 13 and older with listening among EV drivers and riders. AM/FM accounted for 53 percent of in-car audio time among the overall population, compared with 42 percent among the EV group. Streaming music accounted for 17 percent of listening time overall and 22 percent among EV drivers and riders. The EV audience’s share of in-car listening time spent with podcasts was twice that of the overall population. SiriusXM also had a larger share among the EV group: 20 percent, compared with 16 percent overall.
On the business side of media,
Four major media and technology companies have announced November earnings dates. Qualcomm reports November fourth, followed by iHeartMedia and Skydance on November ninth. Warner Music Group reports November nineteenth. Investors can participate through scheduled conference calls or live webcasts. Find the complete schedule, telephone numbers, access codes and webcast links at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to radio,
Westwood One and Silverloch are teaming up for special Election Day coverage on November third. Dan Bongino, Vince Coglianese, Hayley Caronia and Shawn Farash will deliver updates and commentary across radio, podcasts and streaming. Bongino wraps up the night with a live Rumble special beginning at eight Eastern. For affiliate sales inquiries, contact Susan Stephens, Senior Vice President & General Manager at Westwood One.
In digital media news,
National Basketball Insider Brandon “Scoop B” Robinson is launching a new digital media network in early 2027. The platform will feature five original video and audio programs covering basketball, women's sports, hip-hop, fashion and lifestyle. Crossover Media Group will handle advertising sales, sponsorships and distribution. The venture also plans to hire professionals in video production, broadcasting and digital journalism.
Turning to television,
TEGNA has named Brian Gregory President and General Manager of WCNC in Charlotte and WFMY in Greensboro. Gregory brings nearly 30 years of broadcasting experience and most recently led WVEC in Norfolk, where he expanded local streaming programming. He succeeds Joan Barrett, who was promoted to a regional leadership role.
In music news,
The Academy of Country Music has announced its 2026-2027 Board of Directors and officers. Jeff Krones of CAA will serve as Chair, Becky Gardenhire of WME as President, and Rusty Gaston of Sony Publishing as Vice President. The Board includes 19 newly elected directors and 12 new directors-at-large, with representatives from Audacy, Cumulus, iHeart Country, Spotify and Apple Music.
And finally,
What does it take to build a winning radio station? Brian Wright of Wright Media Group says success starts with three fundamentals: strategy, tactics, and execution. Strong leadership, clear priorities, and consistent follow-through turn good plans into lasting success. Read Wright's full blog at Media Jobs Report dot com.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
